title: The May 1904 Lunch in Manchester Where Rolls First Met Royce
conflicts: Venue disputed: the company, BBC and plaques say the Midland Hotel; Edmunds's own account (via Ed Glinert, I Love Manchester) names a 'Great Central Hotel', History Today says 'Grand Central', and Kelly's 1904 directory lists no such hotel. The story gives the tradition and Edmunds's wording side by side. Rolls's remark to Johnson is 'the greatest motor engineer in the world' (company) or 'the greatest engineer in the world' (The Magic of a Name); the company's version is quoted and attributed. Grace's Guide dates the first Royce car to December 1904, against April 1904 everywhere else; not used. Imported makes differ (Peugeot/Minerva vs Panhard/Orleans/Minerva); story says French and Belgian.
notes: No outcome numbers are relied on. Rolls 'agreed on the spot' (company account) and the written agreement is dated 23 December 1904 (Grace's Guide); both are told. 'Edmunds all but dragged Rolls to Manchester' rests on History Today alone and is attributed to Richard Cavendish. Funding set to mixed: built on Royce's publicly floated electrical firm and Rolls's dealership, with a share issue for the 1906 company.
